rounds.proof_sketch: With variance=1e-6, original inv_std=1/sqrt(1e-6+1e-5)≈301.5, mutated inv_std=1/sqrt(1e-6+1e-2)≈10. For delta=0.001 deviations: original output=±0.3015, mutated=±0.01. Difference=0.29 >> threshold 0.013.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation passed random testing because typical random inputs have variance much larger than both epsilon values (1e-5 and 1e-2), making the epsilon contribution negligible. With variance >> 1e-2, both sqrt(var+1e-5) ≈ sqrt(var+1e-2) ≈ sqrt(var). The mutation only manifests when variance is comparable to or smaller than the epsilon difference (~1e-2).
rounds.kill_strategy: Construct inputs with very small variance (≈1e-6) by using alternating +delta/-delta patterns. This makes the epsilon term dominate the variance computation, exposing the 1000x difference between 1e-5 and 1e-2 epsilon values.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing for numerical stability parameters (epsilon) should include low-variance test cases, not just random distributions. The epsilon parameter specifically guards against near-zero variance, so tests must probe this boundary condition.
rounds.suggested_code:
def generate_inputs(device):
    # Low variance input: alternating +/- 0.001 gives variance = 1e-6
    x = torch.zeros(16, 64, 256, 256, device=device, dtype=torch.float32)
    delta = 0.001
    x[..., ::2] = delta    # Even indices: +0.001
    x[..., 1::2] = -delta  # Odd indices: -0.001
    return [x]
